version.changelog:
No file changes detected for version v3.2.3.

- No updates or modifications introduced in this release.
- Functionality, content, and behavior remain identical to v3.2.0.

llm.summary: This travel skill is provider-specific and disclosed, but it can auto-install an unpinned global CLI, force booking-link outputs, and persist sensitive travel queries in a hidden local log.

dimensions.detail: External CLI/network use is expected for real-time travel data, but the artifacts do not clearly disclose third-party query sharing and the runbook stores raw user travel requests and full command strings, which may include sensitive family and itinerary details.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs installation of @fly-ai/flyai-cli with npm i -g and documents an npx install path from a mutable repository branch, with no version pin, checksum, lockfile, or explicit user approval gate.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions redefine the agent as a CLI executor, forbid knowledge-based answers, and require re-execution when booking links or branding are missing; this is over-scoped for a family travel helper even though real-time data use is purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates optional persistent local state in .flyai-execution-log.json containing raw input and command data, uses shell echo to append generated JSON, and also leaves a globally installed CLI behind; there is no retention, redaction, or secure-write guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Planning family trips through flyai/Fliggy is coherent with the stated purpose, but the skill requires all travel answers to come from flyai output and every result to include a booking link and flyai branding, which narrows user choice beyond ordinary travel assistance.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use it only if you trust the flyai CLI and are comfortable sending travel queries to that provider, receiving provider booking links, and installing a global npm package. Prefer a pinned CLI version, require explicit approval before installation, and disable or redesign the execution log so raw prompts and command strings are not stored.
llm.findings:
[P6] expected: The cited SKILL.md output rules are ordinary formatting and factuality instructions; artifact text does not support direct prompt extraction or system prompt disclosure.
[RP1] unexpected: The README does include a mutable npx install path and unpinned CLI install. A flyai dependency is expected, but the unpinned/global installation path is not sufficiently controlled.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The runbook stores raw user_query and command metadata and allows persistence to a hidden local file without consent, minimization, or retention controls; this is not proportionate for travel planning.
[SSD-3] unexpected: The artifact-backed concern is valid: raw travel prompts and full CLI commands may contain sensitive personal, itinerary, booking, or token data and are retained without redaction.
[T01] unexpected: Using flyai as a data source is expected, but mandatory provider-exclusive answers, booking links, branding, and self-reexecution create overbroad commercial output control.
[T08] unexpected: The artifacts require or recommend unpinned global npm installation and a mutable repository install path, creating a supply-chain and local code-execution risk.
[T09] unexpected: The runbook's shell-based append command can turn generated log content that includes raw user input into shell-parsed text, and the hidden persistent log itself increases data-exposure risk.
